MRI RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multisequence multiplanar MRI of the right knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Anterior cruciate ligament tear ?pending reconstruction

COMPARISON:  Right knee radiographs from [Date].

FINDINGS:

The anterior cruciate ligament is completely torn at its proximal femoral attachment. Its proximal fibers are collapsed in the intercondylar area, balled up and scarred. Distally, there is medial extension of what appears to be tibial  inserting distal ACL fibers or arthrofibrosis which is interposed between the medial aspects of the medial tibiofemoral articular surfaces. This is best seen on series 8, image 11.

There is an 8 mm anterior translation of the posterior cortex of the lateral tibial plateau relative to the posterior cortex of the lateral femoral condyle, in keeping with instability. The anterior cruciate ligament tear is likely long-standing given the absence of any marrow edema to suggest recent bony contusion injury.

The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. The medial and lateral collateral ligaments are intact. Biceps femoris, popliteus tendon and iliotibial band are intact.

Lateral meniscus is intact. There is mild blunting/fraying of the apical free edge of the medial meniscus anterior body-anterior horn junction. No surfacing fluid signal intensity meniscal tear cleft. No paranasal cyst or extrusion.

 No significant chondrosis or morphological chondral defect in the patellofemoral, medial or lateral femoral compartments. No subchondral marrow edema.

The extensor mechanism is intact. 

Small volume of joint fluid is likely within normal physiological limits. No synovitis. No intra-articular loose body. 
No Baker's cyst.


INTERPRETATION:

 Complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. There is suspected arthrofibrosis extending into the medial aspect of the medial tibiofemoral articulation.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Medial knee pain for 2 months.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla extremity system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Trace joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex undersurface tear at the body/posterior horn junction and posterior horn with meniscal extrusion into the inferior gutter.
Medial compartment cartilage: Cartilage heterogeneity and surface fraying along the inner weightbearing femoral articular surface.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Cartilage heterogeneity and surface fraying along the weightbearing central tibial articular surface.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full thickness cartilage fissuring with subchondral cystic change along the upper patellar median ridge, lower central and medial trochlear groove. Cartilage heterogeneity along the lateral patellar facet and trochlear groove.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Intact. Mild chronic MCL bursitis.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal tendinosis.
Patella tendon: Mild proximal tendinosis.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. Lateral patellar translation. Patella alta with an I/S ratio of 1.8. Shallow trochlear morphology. Increased tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 20 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Medial meniscus undersurface tear, as described.
2.	Tricompartmental chondrosis, high-grade in the patellofemoral compartment with underlying patellofemoral maltracking.
